itemText: Add a small stdio MCP package in the repo (name it for what it does, for example tools/anki-batch-mcp) using the MCP SDK already in apps/api, with a parser for the tab-separated Anki export that handles quoted HTML fields and cloze spans.
Implement get_next_batch, confirm_batch and status tools with a batch id handshake, so a batch is deleted from Business.txt only when the caller confirms it was saved.
Register the server in .mcp.json as a stdio entry pointing at the package, with the file path passed as an argument so other exports can reuse it later.
Co-located vitest tests for the parser (plain and cloze notes, empty answers) and for the backup-once and confirm-then-remove rules.
Owns the new stdio package folder, .mcp.json and nothing under apps/api.
Add a scopes text-array column to api_tokens in schema.ts, generate the migration with db:generate and run it with db:migrate, never with push.

Let the token creation script take a --scopes flag so a cards:write-only token can be minted for the import.
Owns apps/api/src/api-token, apps/api/src/db/schema.ts, the new migration, the MCP auth gate and the createMcpServer signature.
Add a create_cards tool next to the other MCP tools that checks the cards:write scope from the auth context before touching the database.
Add a repo that finds or creates the deck's knowledge source by import key, maps the deck to its Business sub-subject, and inserts pending bits with a per-card import key so re-runs are no-ops.

The first get_next_batch call creates Business.txt.bak beside the file and a second run never overwrites it.
get_next_batch returns the requested number of notes with deck label, question and answer parsed out of the tab-separated Anki export, cloze notes included.
confirm_batch removes exactly the returned notes from Business.txt and refuses a batch id it never handed out.
Claude Code lists the server's tools from the committed .mcp.json entry with no secret in the config.

Add a submit_knowledge tool next to the other MCP tools that checks the knowledge:write scope from the auth context, maps the deck to its Business sub-subject id, and inserts pending prose sources with the caller's per-note import keys, skipping keys that already exist.
Update the read-only guard test so submit_knowledge is the one allowed writer and every other tool is still proven read-only.
Integration test: the same batch submitted twice yields one set of sources, and an unknown deck name is refused.
submit_knowledge accepts up to 100 notes, each with a content-derived import key and its raw text, plus a deck name, validated with zod, and returns created and already-present counts.

Each deck name maps to an existing Business sub-subject (Основы to Common, Маркетинг и СММ to Marketing, Продажи to Sales, Финансы и планирование to Finance, Лояльность to Loyalty, Персонал и зарплаты to Hiring) and an unknown deck is refused, not guessed.
Sources are inserted with the caller's import keys and conflicts are skipped per note, so re-sending a batch after a crash adds no rows, proven by an integration test.
A token without knowledge:write gets an isError tool result and the read-only guard test still passes for every other tool.
Write the import runbook: batch size, the three tool calls in order, and how to resume after an interrupted batch using the import keys.
A short runbook in the plan folder states the batch size and the order get_next_batch, submit_knowledge, confirm_batch, with no rewriting step in between.
